decisions.reason: It builds directly on the firm's web-mapping capabilities, and the multiple early releases indicate strong absorptive capacity and active refinement rather than withdrawal risk.
The product is close to the firm's established web-map offer, so its in-house R&D and domain knowledge make it more likely to be improved than discontinued despite limited market evidence so far.
This mobile map control component clearly extends existing geospatial UI expertise, and its prominent positioning with a stated usability improvement supports continuation.
A platform for building GIS solutions is highly related to the firm's core integration and software-engineering competences, making it strategically important and unlikely to be dropped.
Mobile field data capture fits well with the firm's geospatial solution portfolio, and its own product page suggests enough commitment to keep developing it.
As a search extension for web map applications, it is closely related to existing knowledge and reusable architectures, so the firm is likely to retain and iterate it.
